new_roles.title: Director of Manufacturing Operations
new_roles.description:
Airlite Plastics is a premier, privately held, family-owned manufacturer headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska. Our family style and personal culture is what makes Airlite an amazing place to grow and build a successful career. Airlite’s company values of unquestionable integrity and respect and appreciation for each other are at the core of our success! These values set a strong foundation to build on where we can ‘wow’ our customers with innovative products and sustainable solutions and continuously improve our processes and efficiencies.

 

Our product lines include rigid plastic containers and lids for food packaging and cosmetics, dry powder scoops, plastic drink cups, shipping containers, industrial strength insulated concrete forms (ICF) and sustainable permeable paving systems. As pioneers in our industry, focused on sustainable solutions, we strive to provide our customers with top-notch service and quality, which aligns with our award-winning products.

 

As Airlite continues to grow and expand, we are excited to add new roles across our organization to support increasing customer demand and future innovation. This is an exciting time to join our team and be part of a company investing in people, technology, and long-term success.

 

**How would you contribute?**

This role is a contributing member of our team located in Nazareth, PA. As a Director of Operations you are a key to continued growth and success of Airlite. The Director of Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for manufacturing operations across assigned Airlite Locations. This role is responsible for Production, Maintenance, and Engineering and ensures operational strategies, resources, and priorities are aligned with business objectives.

This role will drive operational excellence through strong leadership, development of site leadership teams, continuous improvement, effective use of performance metrics, and disciplined execution. A key focus of this position is building leadership capability throughout the organization by coaching and developing managers and supervisors as the operations continue to grow and evolve. The Director will balance consistent operational expectations across locations while recognizing the unique needs and autonomy of each facility.

**Essential Duties:**

* Provide strategic leadership and direction for Production, Maintenance, and Engineering across the Nazareth and Lakeville facilities.

* Lead, coach, and develop operational leaders, strengthening leadership capability, accountability, decision-making, and succession readiness throughout the organization.

* Establish operational priorities, goals, and KPIs and use performance data to drive accountability and continuous improvement.

* Ensure manufacturing operations consistently achieve objectives related to safety, quality, delivery, productivity, efficiency, and cost.

* Partner with site leadership to develop and execute operational plans that support business growth, capacity requirements, equipment needs, and organizational objectives.

* Drive continuous improvement initiatives that improve manufacturing processes, equipment reliability, labor effectiveness, throughput, and overall operational performance.

* Provide leadership for capital projects, equipment installations, process improvements, and other operational initiatives in partnership with Engineering and Maintenance.

* Evaluate organizational structure, staffing, and leadership needs and develop teams capable of supporting current operations and future growth.

* Promote consistency and sharing of best practices between facilities while allowing each operation to respond effectively to its specific business and manufacturing needs.

* Partner cross-functionally with Quality, Supply Chain, Safety, Human Resources, Finance, Sales, Customer Service, and other functions to resolve issues and achieve business objectives.

* Develop and manage operational budgets, forecasts, capital requirements, and resource plans in alignment with financial and strategic objectives.

* Foster a culture of safety, accountability, collaboration, employee development, continuous improvement, and operational excellence while exemplifying Airlite's Core Values and servant leadership principles.

* Other duties as assigned.

 

**Do you have what it takes?** Airlite Plastics is a versatile employer; complacency is not one of our strengths! We work hard each day to ensure that equipment efficiency and customer satisfaction never leave our line of sight. Successful candidates for the role will possess the following:

 

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Operations Management, Manufacturing, or a related field preferred; equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.
* 10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including significant responsibility for manufacturing operations.
* 5+ years of experience leading managers and/or senior operational leaders.
* Demonstrated experience overseeing multiple operational functions such as Production, Maintenance, and Engineering.
* Experience leading operations across multiple facilities or business units strongly preferred.
* Experience with capital planning, operational budgeting, continuous improvement, and manufacturing performance management.
* Plastics manufacturing, injection molding, extrusion, or related manufacturing experience preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to coach, mentor, and develop managers and emerging leaders.
* Strong business and financial acumen with the ability to understand the impact of operational decisions on overall business performance.
* Ability to effectively lead across multiple facilities, balancing consistent operational expectations with the unique needs of each location.
* Capability to solve complex problems, utilizing strong critical thinking and decision-making skills
* Superior organizational skills and the ability to assemble resources needed to orchestrate multiple projects/activities and accomplish goals
* Model a collaborative leadership style with the ability to build partnerships and influence others into action
* Excellent verbal and written communications skills
* Outstanding presentation and facilitation skills
* Excellent interpersonal skills and consultative approach; tactful in dealing with people at all levels
* Strong sense of urgency, self-motivated and positive
* Flexible and adaptable; able to work in ambiguous situations
* Ability to actively lead change initiatives
* Display highest ethical standards
* Maintain the utmost level of confidentiality in dealing with sensitive information
* Detail oriented, with the ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment

 

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; stand; walk; use hand dexterity to operate office equipment including computer keyboards; reach with hands and arms; and talk and hear. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 15 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee may be exposed to moving mechanical parts. The noise level in the office work environment is typically quiet; when visiting the production floor, the noise level may be loud.

 

**Our Core Values Drive Us!**

 

* Do you conduct yourself with unquestionable integrity?

* Do you demonstrate respect and appreciation for those around you?

* Are you innovative and strive to challenge the status quo?

* Do you strive for continuous improvement and to deliver the “wow” factor?

* Do you care about environmentally sustainable solutions?

* Do you take meaning and pride in a job well done?

 

**What’s in it for you?** ***As a Full-Time employee, you will be eligible for the following benefits:***

 

* Health, dental and vision insurance

* Company paid life insurance

* Company paid short term disability

* Generous 401k match

* Generous Time Off

* Annual company activities

new_roles.description:
**Work Schedule**

Standard (Mon-Fri)

**Environmental Conditions**

Office

**Job Description**

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

**LOCATION**: Currently tied to Morrisville, NC (may be open to other locations). Relocation assistance is NOT provided.

* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
* Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

**DESCRIPTION**:

As a Senior Director of Operations at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you'll manage complex manufacturing operations while driving strategic growth and operational excellence. This key leadership role involves directing production of high-quality products in regulated environments while ensuring exceptional customer service and compliance. You'll optimize end-to-end operations, implement continuous improvement initiatives, and develop high-performing teams aligned with our mission of enabling customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.

Working closely with cross-functional partners, you'll establish and execute strategic plans, drive productivity and efficiency improvements, and support a culture focused on quality, safety and customer success. This role requires strong business acumen to manage P&L responsibilities while scaling operations to meet growing demand. You'll support our PPI (Practical Process Improvement) business system and 4i values - Integrity, Intensity, Innovation and Involvement - while developing talent and building engaged, collaborative teams.

**REQUIREMENTS**:

* Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience, or Bachelor's Degree plus 8 years of experience in operations leadership in regulated manufacturing environments
* Preferred Fields of Study: Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, Business or related technical/scientific field
* Advanced training in continuous improvement methodologies (Six Sigma, Lean)
* Demonstrated P&L management and operational excellence experience at scale
* Strong working knowledge of cGMP, FDA, and other relevant quality/regulatory requirements
* Experience leading and developing large, multi-functional teams
* Experience implementing continuous improvement and lean manufacturing methodologies
* Strong business acumen and analytical capabilities
* Effective communication and influence skills across all organizational levels
* Ability to implement change and deliver results in matrix environments
* Experience with ERP systems and manufacturing technologies
* Strong project management capabilities
* Strategic mindset with ability to balance short and long-term priorities
* Experience in customer/client relationship management
* Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities
* Ability to travel 50-75% as required
* Change management and transformation experience
* Cross-functional collaboration and influence skills
* Financial planning and budget management expertise

We offer competitive remuneration, annual incentive plan bonus scheme, healthcare, company 401k, and a range of employee benefits! Thermo Fisher Scientific offers employment with an innovative, forward-thinking organization, and outstanding career and development prospects. We offer an exciting company culture that stands for integrity, intensity, involvement, and innovation.

Thermo Fisher Scientific is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided a reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform critical job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request an accommodation.

**Company Description**

Table 87 Frozen LLC is a national frozen pizza manufacturer and “The Home Of The Coal Oven Slice.” Born in Brooklyn NY, founder Thomas Cucco opened his first slice shop in Brooklyn Heights in 2012. Today, Table 87 runs three authentic coal-oven pizza shops while operating its own vertically integrated frozen production facility that ships its signature frozen pizza nationwide. After national exposure on ABC’s Shark Tank, Table 87 has scaled into top retailers and distributors across the USA, bringing authentic Brooklyn NY coal-oven pizza to freezers everywhere.

**Role Description**

The Director of Operations, Frozen is a full-time, on-site role based in Brooklyn, NY. This role will own day-to-day operations of the Frozen Production Facility and drive consistent output across all frozen manufacturing. Core responsibilities include production leadership, packaging, staffing, inventory and supply-chain optimization, logistics expertise, food-safety elevation, and full facility/equipment readiness. Our mandate is clear: take a high-growth disruptor brand’s production operation and turn it into a dominant, scalable food-manufacturing engine. Success in this role is designed to evolve into COO.

**Qualifications**

* Proven track record evolving an emerging brand into advanced, large-scale manufacturing success
* Proven blend of entrepreneurial grit and disciplined management systems
* Operations leadership experience in food manufacturing or closely related industry

* Ideally experienced in developing and managing SQF certification

* Bachelor’s degree in Operations Management, Food Science, or related field preferred

Pay: $150,000.00 - $200,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance

Education:

new_roles.title: Director of Engineering (Food Manufacturing Plants)
new_roles.description:
**Director of Engineering (Food Manufacturing)**

Dessert Holdings is the leading premium dessert company in the world. We craft artisanal, scratch-made desserts at scale, combining culinary innovation with the finest real ingredients. With a rich heritage spanning seven distinctive brands, we bring unmatched expertise and tailored solutions to our Retail and Foodservice partners.

Dessert Holdings is looking for a **Director of Engineering**to be based in **Aurora, CO** or ideally near one of our production facilities, who will travel as needed to sites for projects. Under the direction of the VP of Engineering & Reliability and in coordination with Corporate and Site Management teams, this individual will provide technical and professional leadership for project management and engineering across Dessert Holdings' tenFood Manufacturing Plants. This role is responsible for capital projects and for identifying, vetting, and championing new manufacturing opportunities and new or emerging technical advancements. This position requires strong personal initiative to identify opportunities, achieve engineering standardization, and implement asset and process best practices within the Dessert Holdings manufacturing facilities.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Provide engineering counsel and leadership for multiple facilities and internal and external project engineers.
* Manage and execute all facets of Dessert Holdings capital projects such as building expansions, and capacity expansion including brownfield and greenfield projects.
* Identify and champion cost reduction projects (capital and non-capital) through process or equipment improvements, capital automation, and robotic opportunities.
* Define technology and manufacturing capabilities to support new business and line extensions.
* Aid with developing 3/5-Year Capital Plan, including originating capital appropriation requests, developing project schedules and work teams, writing of contracts, coordinating project activities, controlling project funds, and implementing startup/training procedures as necessary.
* Write capital projects that include preparation of studies, proposals, estimates, technical reports, capital required, cash flow on approved CEA format.
* Assist in the development and implementation of new facility planning and construction. Includes developing packages, creating equipment and construction specifications, establishing and tracking project budgets, utility utilization, EPA and OSHA requirements, knowledge of GMP's, writing and justifying projects.
* Administer project bid documents and assist with rewarding contracts to outside vendors, architects, and engineers.
* Create and maintain the appropriate engineering records including equipment records and manuals, drawings and diagrams, inspection reports and legal records as required by the appropriate agencies.
* Maintain effective reporting and communication with the appropriate people both within and outside of the plant.
* Work closely with outside agencies in their respective fields, i.e., OSHA, EPA, FDA, etc., to ensure plant compliance with current regulations.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering required or equivalent technical degree. Substantial applicable experience will also be considered.
* 10-15 years of engineering leadership with progressive technical and/or management experience including project management and extensive food manufacturing experience
* Ability to travel up to 75%, throughout the US (8 sites) and Canada (2 sites)
* Hands on approach to problem solving with creative solutions and ability to handle ambiguity
* Strong oral and written communication skills
* Understand business implications of decisions, align work with strategic goals
* Ability to prioritize and plan work activities, set goals, timelines, and objectives
* Display original thinking, creativity and resourcefulness to generate innovative approaches and ideas
* Ability to create and drive automation opportunities including robotic manufacturing capability
* Possess leadership skills and the ability to effectively manage and communicate with engineers, construction personnel, project managers, clients and executives
* Demonstrated proficiency in Word, Excel, Gantt, Power Point, AutoCAD, and project planners
* Familiarity with controls, process, packaging, electrical, mechanical, refrigeration systems
* Knowledge of six sigma and Lean Manufacturing principles

**About Dessert Holdings**

Dssert Holdings is a collection of premium dessert companies and brands: The Original Cakerie, Lawler's Desserts, Atlanta Cheesecake Company, Steven Charles, Dianne's Fine Desserts, Kenny's Great Pies, and Willamette Valley Pie Company. Dessert Holdings is owned by Bain Capital, is headquartered in St. Paul, Minnesota, employs more than 3,500 people across ten manufacturing facilities, and is continuing its journey of rapid growth.

**EEO Statement**

Dessert Holdings and its related entities provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, or any other characteristics protected by law.

new_roles.title: Director of Quality
new_roles.description:
**Company Overview**

Red 6 is an innovative Augmented Reality (AR) technology startup leading the way in synthetic air combat training. Our primary technology, supporting our ATARS product, enables pilots to simulate the cognitive challenges of flying while accessing realistic, scalable training in dynamic outdoor environments.

**Director of Quality**

Lead Red 6 into a scalable aerospace product organization.

Red 6 develops advanced augmented reality capabilities for aerospace and defense applications. We seek a hands-on, strategic Director of Quality to lead the next phase of our evolution into disciplined, repeatable product qualification and production. This leader will strengthen existing foundations while guiding the processes, evidence, and behaviors needed to meet customer, regulatory, safety, and aerospace industry expectations.

Success requires more than maintaining certifications. The Director will embed quality planning into product development, improve manufacturing and supplier readiness, and create a culture in which teams jointly solve problems before they become defects, delays, or compliance findings. Key results are building practical, auditable quality processes with Quality as a trusted partner across Engineering, Operations, Programs, and the supplier base.

**WHAT YOU WILL LEAD**

* Own the enterprise Quality strategy and roadmap, scaling the Quality Management System (QMS) to match product maturity, production volume, and customer commitments.
* Maintain and continuously improve AS9100 certification and audit readiness. Lead management reviews, internal audits, corrective action effectiveness, risk based thinking, and process ownership.
* Lead ISO 45001 occupational health and safety management system maturation and certification readiness, in coordination with accountable safety and operations leaders.
* Deploy practical Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) disciplines aligned to AS9145 where applicable, including quality planning, process flow, PFMEA, control plans, measurement system analysis, first article inspection, and production readiness reviews.
* Integrate Quality into design inputs, reviews, verification and validation, configuration control, design changes, manufacturing transitions, and product release criteria.
* Establish scalable document and record controls, product pedigree, serial level traceability, inspection and test evidence, nonconformance controls, material review, CAPA, and calibration systems.
* Develop supplier qualification, surveillance, performance scorecards, supplier corrective actions, and risk based oversight of contract manufacturers and critical suppliers.
* Partner with Engineering and Operations to strengthen hardware quality, reliability, manufacturability, process validation, FOD/ESD controls, and handling of nonconforming material.
* Improve the connection between Windchill PLM, Epsilon3 MES, Unanet ERP, and existing compliance tools to support controlled, usable, auditable data across design, build, and delivery.
* Lead customer quality engagement, audits, contractual quality deliverables, and coordination with defense and aerospace stakeholders as applicable.

**LEAD A COLLABORATIVE QUALITY CULTURE**

* Build a capable Quality team with clear roles, coaching, succession planning, and cross functional influence.
* Act as a constructive partner to Engineering. Translate standards and contractual obligations into design intent, risk, and measurable acceptance criteria rather than relying on clause citations alone.
* Distinguish nonnegotiable compliance outcomes from implementation choices. Invite Engineering and Operations to co-design efficient solutions.
* Create early quality engagement in program planning and design reviews. Resolve disagreements using evidence, risk, cost, schedule, and accountable decision ownership.
* Establish shared performance measures and a regular Quality–Engineering working cadence to reduce late surprises and unproductive escalation.
* Promote a just, learning oriented culture that encourages timely issue reporting, root cause analysis, and effective preventive action.

**QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
* Significant progressive aerospace or defense quality leadership experience, including building or scaling an AS9100 QMS and leading certification or surveillance audits.
* Demonstrated success moving products from prototype or development environments into qualified, controlled, repeatable production.
* Working knowledge of APQP per AS9145, AS9102 first article inspection, supplier quality, configuration management, CAPA, and risk based process control.
* Ability to influence senior technical leaders without defaulting to authority or unnecessary bureaucracy. Strong facilitation, coaching, and conflict resolution skills.
* Experience with customer and supplier quality requirements, quality metrics, and cross functional improvement programs.

* Ability to work on site in Denver and travel periodically to suppliers and other Red 6 locations.
* Must be US Citizen to have the ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Security Clearance.

**PREFERRED EXPERIENCE**

* ISO 45001 implementation or certification leadership; AS9115 awareness for deliverable software where relevant.
* DoD prime contractor interfaces, DCMA, DFARS, and applicable government customer quality requirements.
* Experience with PLM, MES, ERP, and integrated digital quality workflows, especially Windchill, Epsilon3, and Unanet.
* Lean Six Sigma, ASQ quality credentials, GD&T, hardware reliability, and complex electromechanical systems.
* Experience developing small teams into mature, business enabling quality organizations.

**WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN THE FIRST 12 MONTHS**

* Publish an agreed risk based Quality maturity roadmap with clear process owners and milestones.
* Sustain AS9100 compliance and close systemic audit or corrective action gaps with evidence of effectiveness.
* Introduce an appropriate APQP and production readiness framework for priority product lines.
* Improve supplier quality visibility, product traceability, and readiness of controlled manufacturing documentation.

new_roles.title: Director of Chemistry, Small Molecule Process Development and Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
**About This Role**
 
We are seeking a highly motivated and creative Director of Chemistry to join our Small Molecule Chemical Development team. In this role, you will lead and mentor scientific and engineering teams as you guide project progression from early-phase through late-phase drug development. You will oversee the design and refinement of robust manufacturing processes for a wide range of small molecules, supporting pre - clinical and clinical therapeutics. This role is integral to advancing our scientific endeavors, driving innovation, and enabling the successful launch of new medicines through collaborative, safe, economical, and sustainable process development.

**Who We Are**

We are a team of organic chemists and chemical engineers engaged in the design of innovative processes which supply new medicines to patients. We focus on developing safe, economical, sustainable, cost - effective , and robust processes to support clinical trials and the launch of new medicines across various drug modalities. We are driven by first principles science, data-driven decision-making, and collaborative teamwork.

**What** **You’ll****Do**

* Lead c ollaborat ive development and manufacturing teams to design and conduct experiments to optimize and characterize the processes of Biogen assets with an emphasis on improvement in process understanding, robustness, and productivity.

* D esign, guide and execute experimental plans to advance the Biogen portfolio. You will be responsible for leading project teams towards the implementation of safe, efficient and robust chemical processes Biogen drug candidates. You will c ollaborate with development and manufacturing teams to optimize and characterize the processes of Biogen assets with an emphasis on improvement in process understanding, robustness, and productivity.

* Responsible for managing scientific colleagues, and mentoring, engaging, and preparing our future scientific and engineering leaders

* Develop the fundamental process knowledge needed to support the transition of chemical and biochemical processes from laboratory scale to manufacturing partners.

* Collaborate with our Process Engineering, Analytical Chemistry, Oligo Synthesis, Solid Form, and Separations colleagues to develop the knowledge and controls needed for the supply of clinical materials and characterization of processes to support regulatory filings.

* Communicate project team research results effectively by in reports and discussions in team meetings , including e ngage ment in CMC activities including authoring CMC section of INDs.

* Interact with Contract Research Organizations as project needs evolve , which may include travel

* Initiate innovative research projects to improve fundamental understanding and control of Biogen processes

* Expand on your Chemistry community presence professionally representing Biogen externally in consortia and conferences

**Who You Are**

You have a passion for exploring scientific concepts and are eager to contribute to the design and development and execution of cutting-edge technologies in the service of delivering drug cand idates for clinical trials . Your vision and dedication drive you to push the boundaries of scientific endeavors, ultimately impacting patient lives. You thrive in a collaborative environment where urgency, accountability, inclusion and integrity are shared value s .

* M.S. or PhD with 12 + years of relevant experience , including people management, in pharmaceutical or biotech settings is required

* Strong background in the theory and practice of pharmaceutical process chemistry and engineering , including command of synthetic strategies, impurity controls, analytical, purification and isolation techniques, process characterization , familiarity with process safety and tech transfer protocols, and good problem -s olving skills in the service of delivering non-clinical and clinical APIs and the phase appropriate knowledge packages for CMC support.

* Demonstrated experience in leading project teams involved in delivery of APIs across several modalities

* Ability to lead teams ethically, collaboratively , effectively, and cross-functionally

* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills are required along with the desire to work in a highly collaborative team environment .

**Preferred Skills:**

* Experience in engaging with external partners and representing the organization in external facing settings.

* Familiarity with regulatory requirements and CMC activities related to drug development.

 
Job Level: Management 

**Additional Information**

The base compensation range for this role is: $188,000.00-$258,500.00 

Base salary offered is determined through an analytical approach utilizing a combination of factors including, but not limited to, relevant skills & experience, job location, and internal equity.

 

Regular employees are eligible to receive both short term and long-term incentives, including cash bonus and equity incentive opportunities, designed to reward recent achievements and recognize your future potential based on individual, business unit and company performance.

 
 

In addition to compensation, Biogen offers a full and highly competitive range of benefits designed to support our employees’ and their families *physical, financial, emotional,* and *social well-being* ; including, but not limited to:

* Medical, Dental, Vision, & Life insurances
* Fitness & Wellness programs including a fitness reimbursement
* Short- and Long-Term Disability insurance
* A minimum of 15 days of paid vacation and an additional end-of-year shutdown time off (Dec 26-Dec 31)
* Up to 12 company paid holidays + 3 paid days off for Personal Significance
* 80 hours of sick time per calendar year
* Paid Maternity and Parental Leave benefit
* 401(k) program participation with company matched contributions
* Employee stock purchase plan
* Tuition reimbursement of up to $10,000 per calendar year
* Employee Resource Groups participation
 

 

**Why Biogen?**

We are a global team with a commitment to excellence, and a pioneering spirit. As a mid-sized biotechnology company, we provide the stability and resources of a well-established business while fostering an environment where individual contributions make a significant impact. Our team encompasses some of the most talented and passionate achievers who have unparalleled opportunities for learning, growth, and expanding their skills. Above all, we work together to deliver life-changing medicines, with every role playing a vital part in our mission. Caring Deeply. Achieving Excellence. Changing Lives.

 
 

At Biogen, we are committed to building on our culture of inclusion and belonging that reflects the communities where we operate and the patients we serve. We know that diverse backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives make us a stronger and more innovative company, and we are focused on building teams where every employee feels empowered and inspired.

 
 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, marital status, race, color, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, religion, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information or any other basis protected by federal, state or local law. Biogen is an E-Verify Employer in the United States.

**About the Position**

HFVCO is looking for an accomplished manufacturing leader to take ownership of plant performance within a food or beverage production environment. The Plant Manager will guide department leadership, oversee financial and operational results, and establish priorities that strengthen safety, product quality, output, reliability, and cost performance.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Direct plant-wide activities across production, maintenance, quality, warehousing, shipping, and safety

* Develop department managers and supervisors through coaching, accountability, and performance management
* Lead operational improvement initiatives focused on efficiency, equipment utilization, waste reduction, and plant performance

* Coordinate and support customer, corporate, and regulatory inspections and audits

* Experience with facility budgets, cost management, operational metrics, and financial performance
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes and continuous improvement practices
* Working knowledge of GMPs, sanitation, food safety, and regulatory compliance
* Demonstrated ability to lead, coach, and develop manufacturing teams

new_roles.title: Plant Manager - TimberPro
new_roles.description:
**Join Komatsu and Be Part of Something Big!**

**Job Overview**
----------------

Planning, organizing, leading and controlling all manufacturing related activities of TimberPro Inc. (TPI). Responsible for the performance of departmental functions: Manufacturing, Materials Management, Quality Assurance, Production Planning, CapEx Planning, Human Resources, Facilities Management and supporting Manufacturing Engineering.

**Key Job Responsibilities**
----------------------------

* Develops, reviews, and approves operating plans to achieve production and financial objectives, with accountability for budget control, labor and material efficiency, customer service, order fulfillment, employee relations, and effective workforce utilization.
* Manages Material Resource Planning (MRP), including inventory planning, accuracy, control, and optimization. Coordinates with major suppliers to ensure accurate forecasting, appropriate inventory levels, and reliable component availability to meet production requirements and future capacity expansion.
* Monitors performance against operating plans and standards, communicates results, identifies areas requiring corrective action, and recommends adjustments to achieve operational objectives.
* Develops and presents monthly performance reports as requested by Executive management.
* Develops and implements local policies and procedures consistent with corporate standards, regulatory requirements, OSHA standards, and Komatsu safety requirements, ensuring compliance and a strong safety culture.
* Establishes plant operating objectives and develops short- and long-term plans, budgets, financial forecasts, and resource requirements to achieve business goals.
* Provides oversight for plant cost control, cost forecasting, workforce planning, and facility and capacity requirements, identifying risks and implementing actions to achieve operational and financial objectives.
* Reviews and approves the development and review of all TPI manufacturing budgets.
* Manages facility contracts and third-party service providers, including material disposal, plant and facility maintenance, uniforms, and other site services, ensuring cost, service, and compliance performance.
* Oversees plant budgeting, reviews departmental budget proposals, monitors spending, and authorizes expenditures within established approval limits.
* Reviews and approves major projects involving functional changes within TPI.
* Leads identification and implementation of new manufacturing technologies, automation, processes, and capabilities supporting TimberPro’s long-term operational strategy. Collaborates across Komatsu manufacturing operations to leverage best practices, technical expertise, and solutions that drive improvement in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity.
* Consults with management responsible for policy or action, ensures compliance within areas of responsibility, and recommends improvements to policies and procedures.
* Establishes objectives and procedures governing assigned activities. Issues annual objectives to immediate subordinates and reviews objectives of TPI management.
* Builds and maintains an effective plant leadership team through selection, development, coaching, and retention of qualified personnel. Ensures clear roles, responsibilities, and accountability and supports compensation, training, performance management, and succession planning.
* Leads and evaluates direct reports, coordinates activities across functions, identifies training and development needs, and takes appropriate personnel actions to ensure organizational performance.
* Maintains effective communication with employees at all plant levels, providing clear direction, timely feedback, and visibility to business priorities and operational performance.
* Ensures coordination across plant functions and other company organizations, resolving cross-functional issues related to new product development, workers’ compensation, inventory control, and operational performance.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications/Requirements**
-------------------------------

* Bachelor’s Degree Manufacturing, Engineering or Business Required. MBA or Masters in Engineering or Manufacturing preferred.
* Minimum 3 years’ experience as a GM of Operations in Manufacturing or similar experience.
* Sound administrative skills, well-developed management skills – principles and people.
* Strong communication skills with the ability to effectively communicate across all functions of the organization.
* Working experience in union and non-union environments.
* Experience with Material Management – Bills of Materials, Sourcing, Purchasing, and Inventory Management.
* Experience with new product development and transitioning those products into production.
* Proven ability to recruit, train, and motivate personnel in order to gain profitability and strengthen the organization.
* Honest and trustworthy toward all members of the organization. Use discretion on matters of confidentiality.
* Portray an optimistic and positive attitude in dealings with peers and subordinates.

**Company Benefits**

Komatsu provides an extensive and robust employee benefits package that is designed to enhance the well-being of our employees and family members. We embrace a positive and empowering employee experience with a culture that prides itself on a diverse and inclusive environment.

* Health benefits: Medical, dental, vision, HSA, wellness programs, etc.
* 401k and/or employee savings programs
* Employee time off (vacation and designated holidays)
* Employee and family assistance programs
* Disability benefits
* Life insurance
* Employee learning and development programs

**Diversity & Inclusion Commitment**

At Komatsu, we come from diverse backgrounds, with unique perspectives, experiences, and contributions. We are committed to creating a workforce that is reflective of the communities we work and live in. We believe that our people are part of our shared purpose. Connected by our core values of ambition, perseverance, collaboration and authenticity, we are committed to continually advancing in our support of diversity and inclusion. United, we are on a journey towards a sustainable future that creates value together.

**Company Information**

Komatsu develops and supplies technologies, equipment and services for the construction, mining, forklift, industrial and forestry markets. Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, Komatsu employs more than 64,000 people worldwide, operating in more than 140 countries. For more than a century, the company has been creating value for its customers through manufacturing and technology innovation, partnering with others to empower a sustainable future where people, business and the planet thrive together. Since the company’s founding in 1921, Komatsu has been committed to supporting individuals and communities through job training, skills development and giving back. As a Komatsu employee, you will be encouraged to grow alongside our global company, contributing to a more sustainable future for all. If you are looking for a company that values your talent and potential, join Komatsu to be a part of something big and help advance modern society. Learn more at www.komatsu.com.

**EEO Statement**

Komatsu is an Equal Opportunity Workplace and an Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

It takes an incredible team to deliver the goodness of dairy and enrich our communities – come join us!

**GENERAL PURPOSE**

Direct and coordinate overall plant operations and priorities, and through managers, supervisors, and staff, ensure product is produced efficiently and within cost parameters. Provide work direction to management and employees within the guidelines of standard work rules, union contract provisions (if applicable), and employment policies. Is held accountable for achieving the plant's key performance indicators. Support the Continuous Improvement (CI) initiative to improve productivity, quality, efficiency of operations, and the facility's culture. Manage the overall operating budget including capital and expense projects. Direct personnel activities of department, such as recruitment, hiring, performance evaluations, and salary adjustments using independent judgment within the framework of established human resources policies and practices.

This plant manager job is a single incumbent role responsible for multiple plants or a large and/or complex plant that may also have an assistant plant manager(s) within the plant.

**JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Manage plant operations in all areas of responsibility including administration, production, processing, packaging, quality, maintenance, warehousing, shipping, purchasing, safety, and environmental

* Establish production priorities to ensure product is produced efficiently and within cost parameters while maintaining safety, quality and sanitation standards; obtain optimum production and utilization of workforce, machines, and equipment

* Review and analyze production, quality control, maintenance, and operational reports to ensure compliance and determine causes of non-conformity with product specifications, customer requirements, FDA/government regulations, etc. Report any non-compliance immediately per established protocol

* Analyze plant operations to ensure that the facility maintains a leadership position in the industry and that it takes advantage of new processes and technologies that become available

* Interact with customers to meet their expectations on a variety of goals including operational, customer service, financial, and quality

* Develop, monitor, and drive plant key performance indicators (KPI's) related to safety, quality, productivity and finances. Strive for continuous improvement in KPI results. Promote continuous improvement culture and activities

* Understand plant P&L to drive plant performance; participate in the development of annual operating, capital and expense budgets; provide reliable and accurate information to finance to meet end-of-month closing schedules

* Manage or oversee all corporate, customer, and government audits to ensure compliance

* Conduct meetings with management and staff to ensure all operational issues are being communicated and addressed expediently with a common understanding of goals

* Communicate company goals and assist in establishing objectives that align with plant and company goals; communicate plant direction, focus and goals

* Provide appropriate direction, mentoring, training, and development planning for managers. Identify and retain highly effective personnel through proper selection, training and task assignment. Actively work with direct reports to cultivate capabilities and utilize strengths to support career development and succession planning efforts

* Maintain safe working conditions for employees and compliance with all company, state and federal regulations regarding health and safety issues

* Follow all DFA good manufacturing practices (GMP) and work in a manner consistent with all company regulatory, food safety, quality, and sanitation requirements

* The requirements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by employee, but is not a complete list of responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Other duties may be assigned as required

**BENEFITS:**

* Health and Welfare benefits begin 1st of the month after start date
* 401(k) with company contribution – 100% vested at day one of eligibility
* Competitive pay
* Paid vacation and holidays
* Career growth opportunities – we promote from within!
* Comprehensive healthcare benefits
* Service recognition and employee rewards
* Employee referral program
* Tuition reimbursement
* Work for dairy farm families

Requirements:

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE**

* High school diploma or equivalent

* Undergraduate degree in related curriculum preferred

* 8 or more years' experience in a manufacturing environment, preferably dairy/ESL manufacturing

* 2 or more years' plant management experience

* Experience in union environments preferred

* Proven track record of improved results in the areas of quality, safety, service and cost

* Certification and/or License – may be required during course of employment

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES**

* Strong knowledge of manufacturing process flow and importance to process

* Strong knowledge of continuous improvement models

* Thorough understanding of regulatory laws and responsibilities as it relates to facility standards

* Proficient understanding of budgeting and cost control

• Skill in leadership and coaching; strong knowledge of principles and practices of supervision, training, and personnel management • Knowledge of and skill with Microsoft Office Suite and company computer systems

* Skill in critical thinking, analysis, mathematical calculations, and statistical evaluations

* Able to work in collaboration effectively and foster good teamwork

* Able to interact positively and work effectively with others (interpersonal skills)

* Able to think and use independent judgment in planning and organizing multiple tasks and information

* Able to demonstrate strong initiative

* Able to take appropriate steps to find solutions to problems

* Able to present options and ideas to current processes or procedures

* Able to handle challenging or conflict situations with tact and professionalism

* Able to communicate with various levels of personnel to ensure customers' needs and requirements are met

* Able to interpret and apply company policies

* Able to adapt and manage to change effectively

* Must be able to read, write and speak English

An Equal Opportunity Employer including Disabled/Veterans

 
 
Compensation: $175000 - $190000 / year

new_roles.title: Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
**What you’ll do:**
-------------------

Eaton's Electrical Sector Americas - ARS/Fibrebond division is currently seeking a Plant Manager for its manufacturing operations in Minden, Louisiana. This role is a critical member of the site leadership team and is responsible for leading safe, high-quality, on-time, and cost-effective operations. Relocation assistance is available to candidates currently residing in the U.S. 
 
In this role, you will lead the Minden manufacturing site and its leadership team. You will drive strategic and operational initiatives including plant P&L, growth strategy, capacity, execution, and the direction of the team to meet and exceed short- and long-term business goals. You will foster an environment of engagement and inclusion for all employees and act with advocacy, empathy, and accountability. 
 
Fibrebond, an Eaton company, designs and manufactures pre-integrated modular buildings and power enclosures that protect mission-critical equipment for data center, industrial, utility, and communications customers. Headquartered in Minden, Louisiana, Fibrebond is known for its engineered-to-order solutions that support complex infrastructure projects across North America. In 2025, Fibrebond was acquired by Eaton, expanding Eaton's modular solutions portfolio while preserving Fibrebond's strong engineering expertise, customer focus, and manufacturing operations in Louisiana. 
 
**What you’ll need:** 

* Develop short- and long-term plans in alignment with the strategic plan and annual profit plan objectives to drive superior operational performance and financial results.
* Lead the operational management team and functional staff including Quality, OPEX, EHS and Supply Chain.
* Establish objectives and drive Key Performance Indicators across the organization ensuring continuous improvement.
* Emphasize utilization of Lean/Six Sigma manufacturing tools (Kaizen, VSM, 5S+) to lead cost improvement
* Establish and manage inventory to profit plan, driving improved and sustainable processes; execute the Supply Demand Planning (SIOP), drive ownership and collaboration across all stakeholder groups; generate forecasts that meet customer expectations.
* Champion a workplace focused on Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) to drive a zero-incident safety culture.
* Focus on Quality, early detection and escalations across the site to reduce cost, drive efficiency and ensure compliance.
* Create a culture of exceeding customer expectations, ensuring that the organization is highly responsive to customer needs.
* Demonstrate the ability to be innovative by developing and implementing creative solutions to complex problems, fostering a culture of innovation and continuously seeking opportunities for improvement.
* Partner with Human Resources to drive talent management, learning, communication, and development strategies.
* Champion and advocate for a winning plant culture aligned with the Eaton Culture Model

**Qualifications:**
-------------------

**Required Qualifications:** 

* Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited institution
* 10+ years of experience with progressive levels of accountability and responsibility in roles focused on manufacturing, supply chain, finance, OPEX and/or related support functions in a manufacturing environment.
* 5+ years of people-management experience
* Must be able to travel as business needs require.
* Eaton will not consider applicants for employment immigration sponsorship or support for this position.This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc.

 
**Preferred Qualifications:** 

* MBA from an accredited institution
* Previous experience leading a complex engineered-to-order manufacturing operation through growth, capacity expansion, operational transformation.
* Plant P&L leadership experience with strong business acumen.
* 3+ years of experience as a leader of leaders.

**Additional Information**
--------------------------

* This role will be based at our Fibrebond manufacturing plant in Minden, LA.
* Relocation will be offered for this position.

All positions may require participation in video and in-person interviews as part of the hiring process. All candidates will be evaluated based on job-related competencies, and all candidates’ privacy rights and data security will be protected in accordance with applicable laws.

At Eaton, we strive to provide compensation and benefits that attract, engage, and retain the best talent. This includes competitive pay and a variety of benefit programs for eligible employees. The expected annual salary range for this role is $182000 - $266000 a year. This role is also eligible for a variable incentive program. *Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.*

We are committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of an applicant's race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, marital status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by law.

Eaton believes in second chance employment. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction history will be considered regardless of their arrest or conviction history, consistent with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act and other local laws.

You do not need to disclose your conviction history or participate in a background check until a conditional job offer is made to you. After making a conditional offer and running a background check, if Eaton is concerned about conviction that is directly related to the job, you will be given the chance to explain the circumstances surrounding the conviction, provide mitigating evidence, or challenge the accuracy of the background report.

To request a disability-related reasonable accommodation to assist you in your job search, application, or interview process, please call us at 1-800-836-6345 to discuss your specific need. Only accommodation requests will be accepted by this phone number.

We know that good benefit programs are important to employees and their families. Eaton provides various Health and Welfare benefits as well as Retirement benefits, and several programs that provide for paid and unpaid time away from work. Click here for more detail: Eaton Benefits Overview. Please note that specific programs and options available to an employee may depend on eligibility factors such as geographic location, date of hire, and the applicability of collective bargaining agreements.

new_roles.title: Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
**Plant Manager – Furniture Manufacturing**

**Position Summary**

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on, and results-driven **Plant Manager** to lead our furniture manufacturing operations. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced manufacturing leader to take ownership of plant performance, develop a strong leadership team, improve production processes, and make a direct impact on the success and growth of the facility.

The Plant Manager will oversee all aspects of plant operations, including production, safety, quality, scheduling, cost management, and employee development. This individual will provide leadership and oversight to department supervisors across the facility, ensuring all departments work together to achieve production, quality, safety, and operational goals.

The ideal candidate is a strong, people-focused leader with a solid manufacturing background who knows how to motivate teams, develop supervisors, improve processes, solve problems, and create a culture of accountability, teamwork, safety, and quality.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Plant Operations & Production**

* Direct and oversee daily manufacturing operations to ensure production goals, quality standards, and delivery expectations are consistently met.
* Coordinate activities across departments to maximize productivity, efficiency, and workflow.
* Identify and implement process improvements to reduce waste, control labor costs, and increase operational efficiency.
* Develop and monitor production goals, performance metrics, and operational procedures.
* Oversee equipment needs, maintenance coordination, and resource planning to support production demands.

**Leadership & Employee Development**

* Provide overall leadership, direction, and oversight to department supervisors across all areas of the manufacturing plant.
* Lead, coach, and develop supervisors to ensure effective management of their respective departments and teams.
* Establish clear performance expectations, goals, and accountability for department supervisors.
* Monitor departmental performance and work with supervisors to address challenges, improve productivity, and achieve production goals.
* Oversee employee training and development initiatives to build a skilled, productive workforce.
* Promote teamwork, communication, and collaboration between departments to ensure smooth and efficient plant operations.
* Foster a positive work environment focused on employee engagement, accountability, safety, quality, and continuous improvement.

**Cost Management & Financial Performance**

* Develop and manage plant budgets while maintaining effective cost controls.
* Identify opportunities to reduce labor and production costs without sacrificing quality or safety.
* Implement and maintain production cost tracking systems to evaluate manufacturing performance.
* Monitor labor utilization, productivity, and operating expenses to support profitability.

**Safety & Quality**

* Promote a safe working environment and ensure employees follow established safety procedures.
* Maintain high standards for product quality and accuracy throughout the manufacturing process.
* Monitor production processes and implement improvements to reduce defects, waste, and product returns.
* Ensure the facility has the necessary supplies, equipment, and resources to maintain safe and efficient operations.

**Systems & Process Improvement**

* Work closely with office personnel to improve administrative processes, reporting systems, and documentation.
* Establish and maintain effective production records and reporting procedures.
* Stay current with manufacturing technology, equipment, and industry best practices.
* Support improvements to systems and processes that enhance product quality, operational efficiency, and customer service.
* Perform other duties as needed to support the success of plant operations.

**Qualifications & Experience**

**Required Qualifications:**

* High school diploma or equivalent.
* Minimum of 5 years of manufacturing, production, scheduling, or operations experience.
* Minimum of 3 years of leadership or supervisory experience in a manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated ability to lead supervisors and teams, manage performance, and drive operational results.
* Strong problem-solving, organizational, communication, and decision-making skills.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* 5–7 years of manufacturing operations or production management experience.
* Previous Plant Manager, Operations Manager, Production Manager, or similar leadership experience.
* Experience in furniture manufacturing or a similar production environment.
* Experience managing multiple departments and supervising department leaders.
* Experience managing production costs, labor efficiency, budgets, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Bachelor's degree in Business, Manufacturing, Operations Management, or a related field is a plus, but equivalent hands-on experience will be considered.

**Key Skills & Competencies**

* Strong leadership and team-building skills.
* Employee development and performance management.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
* Strong time management and organizational abilities.
* Manufacturing and operational knowledge.
* Results-oriented mindset.
* Problem-solving and continuous improvement.
* Attention to detail and accountability.

**What We Offer**

We value our employees and offer a benefits package designed to support their health, financial well-being, and work-life balance.

* Health Insurance available after 90 days.
* 401(k) retirement plan available after one year.
* Paid vacation.
* Additional company benefits.

**Work Environment & Physical Requirements**

This position operates in a furniture manufacturing facility. The work environment may include exposure to airborne particles, fumes, moving mechanical equipment, vibration, and elevated noise levels.

The position requires frequent standing, walking, reaching, and use of hands. Occasional sitting, climbing, balancing, bending, kneeling, crouching, and crawling may be required.

The ability to regularly lift or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift or move up to 25 pounds is required. Specific vision requirements include close, distance, color, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

* We are conducting a confidential search for a Plant Manager with a well-established industrial manufacturer in the Tulsa area.
* This leader will oversee a concrete production operation and have direct influence over safety, quality, production performance, and the people who make it happen.
* The company is seeking an experienced, hands-on leader who can set expectations, develop teams, and produce consistent results.

**What You Will Lead:**

* Safety first, always. Establish and maintain a proactive safety culture through field presence, training, hazard recognition, and accountability.
* Lead daily plant production, scheduling, staffing, equipment readiness, output, and on-time fulfillment.
* Own quality control and product consistency, including adherence to customer specifications and internal manufacturing standards.
* Oversee concrete manufacturing processes such as batching, reinforcement, forming and molds, casting, curing, handling, and finished-product inspection.
* Coach supervisors, leads, and hourly employees; develop talent and improve workforce performance, engagement, and accountability.
* Partner with maintenance, engineering, and logistics to reduce downtime, rework, waste, and process bottlenecks.

**What We Are Looking For:**

* Demonstrated success leading manufacturing operations with direct accountability for workplace safety, quality, production, and labor.
* Strong practical experience in concrete manufacturing is highly preferred; reinforced concrete pipe, culverts, drainage structures, manholes, inlets, vaults, or related products are especially relevant.
* Knowledge of production processes, quality inspections, equipment, maintenance coordination, and continuous improvement.
* Proven ability to lead frontline teams, strengthen supervisors, and solve operational problems on the plant floor.
* Clear communication, sound judgment, and the ability to balance production goals with uncompromising safety standards.
* Bilingual English and Spanish skills are a significant plus, but not a requirement.

**Compensation and Location:**

* Ensure all production and yard operations meet DVP quality control standards

* Oversee and manage all incoming materials to ensure adequate inventory levels are met
* Continually collect and review data to reduce inefficiencies and waste
* Successfully hire, supervise, train, and retain production/yard staff
* Evaluate and review employee’s performance for the purpose of determining skill level and training needs
* Coach and mentor employees to allow for increased responsibilities and career advancement. Lead by example.
* Promote and maintain a clean work environment
* Recommend purchases of additional equipment for efficiency, cost reductions and/or quality improvements
* Successfully work with Quality Control/Project Management to meet customer demand and expectations
* Perform any other duties as assigned by the General Manager

* Leading by example, create and sustain a safe working environment for the facility

* Strong oral and written communication skills

* Standing and walking for extended periods of time

**About Justrite Safety Group**

At **Justrite Safety Group**, we're more than just a collection of industrial safety companies; we're a dynamic organization dedicated to protecting people, property, and the planet. Our ever-growing portfolio of companies collaborates to deliver advanced industrial safety solutions that set the standard for excellence.

As our business continues to grow, we continue to look for top talent to join our team as we lead the charge in revolutionizing industrial safety, ensuring that every worker returns home safe, every workplace remains secure, and our environment thrives for generations to come. With Justrite Safety Group, safety isn't just a priority—it's our passion.

**The Contribution You'll bring to this Role:**

The Plant Manager is a strategic plant leadership role accountable for the safe, efficient, and compliant operation of one of the Justrite sites responsible for metal fabrication. This role leads daily execution across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, and People (SQDCP) and ensures finished goods are produced to plan to support customer service and inventory targets.

The Plant Manager partners closely with Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, Maintenance, and EHS to stabilize schedules, improve throughput, reduce scrap and rework, and sustain standard work. While there is no centralized warehouse, the Plant Manager ensures effective on-site staging, WIP control, and shipping coordination to support on-time delivery.

**About the Team:**

As a member of our **Operations** team, you will be dedicated to driving efficiency and excellence across all aspects of our business. With a focus on streamlined processes and innovative solutions, they ensure that our operations run smoothly and effectively. Their expertise is key to maintaining our competitive edge and supporting the growth and success of our company.

**What You'll Do at Justrite:**

* Own site safety performance: eliminate hazards, strengthen near-miss reporting, and ensure timely corrective action closure.

* Ensure compliance with OSHA/local regulations, required training, PPE, and audit readiness.

* Lead incident investigations and implement sustainable countermeasures.

**Operations and Delivery Performance**

* Deliver daily and weekly production plan attainment while maintaining schedule stability and rapid issue escalation.

* Manage labor and staffing plans (shift coverage, overtime, cross-training) to meet output and service-level targets.

* Coordinate shipping priorities and finished goods readiness with Customer Service and Supply Chain.

**Quality and Process Control**

* Ensure product conformance to specifications; partner with Quality on containment, root cause, and corrective actions.

* Reduce scrap and rework through process controls, mistake-proofing, training, and layered process audits as applicable.

**Reliability and Continuous Improvement**

* Partner with Maintenance to drive preventive maintenance compliance, uptime, and reliability improvements (TPM where applicable).

* Lead Lean/CI initiatives (5S, standard work, setup reduction, flow improvements) across fabrication and machining.

* Use data-driven problem solving (A3, 5-Why) to improve throughput, OEE, and constraint performance.

**People Leadership and Cost Management**

* Create and deliver on operational plans to achieve budget

* Develop and coach supervisors, managers, and team leads; set expectations, build accountability, and strengthen engagement.

* Own controllable cost drivers (labor, overtime, scrap/rework, supplies) and deliver annual operating plan targets.

* Identify and justify capital, tooling, and automation opportunities with strong ROI.

**Key Interfaces**

* Supply Chain (S&OP, production planning, material availability, inventory targets, expedites)

* Quality (supplier/customer issues, corrective actions, audits)

* Engineering (process improvements, routings/BOM alignment, tooling/fixtures)

* Maintenance (preventive maintenance, downtime root cause, reliability)

* EHS (training, compliance, risk assessments)

**Key Performance Indicators (Typical)**

* Safety: TRIR/recordables, near-miss reporting, corrective action closure

* Delivery: schedule attainment, plan adherence, on-time shipment performance

* Quality: scrap and rework rates, customer complaints/returns, internal defect rate

* Productivity: OEE or key equipment uptime, labor efficiency, throughput, setup/changeover time

* Cost: overtime, conversion cost per unit, premium freight driven by site issues

* People: turnover/attendance, training completion, engagement actions

**Your Skills and Expertise:**

To ensure your success from day one in this role, Justrite requires the following qualifications at a minimum:

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, or related field (or equivalent experience).

* 15+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including leadership of supervisors and production teams.

* Experience in metal fabrication and/or machining operations (CNC and fab processes).

* Demonstrated success improving SQDCP performance using Lean/CI methods.

* Working knowledge of ERP/MRP environments and production reporting.

*Additional qualifications that could help you succeed even further in this role include:*

* Experience in make-to-stock environments with finished goods availability targets and replenishment planning.

* Black Belt certification or equivalent practical experience.

* Experience coordinating outside processing/special processes (heat treat, coating/plating, paint) as applicable.

* Experience with ISO 9001 or similar quality systems.

**Compensation:**

The position offers a competitive base salary ranging from $180,000 to $190,000. This role offers relocation assistance.

Plant Manager – Level 3 Water Treatment PlantNorth Greene Utilities (NGU)Baileyton, Tennessee

North Greene Utilities is seeking a certified Level 3 Water Treatment Plant Manager to lead operations at our Level 3 water treatment production plant in Baileyton Tennessee. This is a key leadership role responsible for the full management of plant functions, regulatory compliance, and a small team of operators.

Position Overview

The Plant Manager oversees all day-to-day and long-term operations of NGU’s Level 3 water treatment plant. The position ensures continuous production of safe, high-quality water that meets or exceeds all Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation (TDEC) and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) standards and guidance. The manager supervises, mentors, and develops a team of three subordinates while maintaining efficient, safe, and compliant plant operations.

Key Responsibilities

* Manage all plant functions and treatment processes to meet TDEC and EPA regulatory requirements and policy guidance.• Supervise, mentor, and train three subordinates. Two subordinates are expected to achieve Level 1 certification by mid-2027.• Develop, implement, and manage shift schedules to ensure continuous, reliable plant coverage.• Ensure compliance with all federal and state safety regulations and NGU safety protocols.• Conduct lifecycle and operational management of treatment infrastructure, including maintenance planning and capital needs.• Participate in daily stand-up meetings with the NGU management team.• Assist with HR requirements for subordinates, including ensuring compliance with company policies.• Monitor the health and welfare of subordinates.• Conduct biannual performance counseling for subordinates.• Demonstrate flexibility and adaptability to evolving operational requirements and tasks as directed by the Operations Supervisor and General Manager.• Maintain accurate records, reporting, and documentation required for regulatory compliance and internal management.

Qualifications

* Current Tennessee Level 3 Water Treatment Operator certification (required).• Proven experience in water treatment plant operations, preferably in a leadership or supervisory role.• Strong knowledge of TDEC and EPA drinking water regulations, treatment processes, and compliance requirements.• Ability to supervise, train, and develop staff.• Valid driver’s license and ability to meet any additional job-related certifications or requirements (e.g., safety, drug and alcohol screening).• Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.• Commitment to safety, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement.

Compensation and Benefits

NGU offers very competitive wages, an IRA, health insurance, and dental coverage. Additional details on pay and benefits will be discussed with qualified candidates.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should submit a resume, copy of current Level 3 certification, and contact information to .
